# DECISION LOG — ARKALI GENESIS v2

Decisions taken during Phase 0 that are not large enough for an ADR, or that record a human ruling. Architectural decisions of consequence live in `docs/adr/ADR_INDEX.md`.

| # | Decision | Rationale | Authority |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-001 | 31 bounded contexts across a 7-layer model | Gives every canonical concern exactly one home and makes dependency direction mechanically checkable | Phase 0A |
| D-002 | Contexts consolidated into 4 architecture documents rather than one file per required artifact | The canonical set lists ~27 required 0A artifacts; coherent grouped documents beat 27 fragments that would drift apart | Phase 0A |
| D-003 | Layer rule: strictly-lower dependencies only, same-layer edges enumerated explicitly | An unenumerated same-layer edge is how cycles appear; making the 7 legitimate edges explicit makes the rest detectable | Phase 0A |
| D-004 | Promotion and rollback split across two lifecycle authorities | Prevents a failed promotion from approving its own recovery | ADR-0009 |
| D-005 | ID ranges allocated sparsely (MS 0001–0186, BP 0200–0243, VDC 0300–0380) | New requirements can be added inside their source block without renumbering; IDs are immutable | Phase 0B |
| D-006 | Minimise CONDITIONAL classification; everything else MANDATORY or OPTIONAL. Current count: **8** | Conditional classification is the main scope-narrowing exploit; every CONDITIONAL entry carries an objective machine-evaluable rule. The count is authoritative in `REQUIREMENT_REGISTER.md`, not here | Phase 0B (count revised by D-014) |
| D-007 | Architecture budgets set deliberately generous (400 logical lines, fan-out 12) | Purpose is catching a central orchestrator, not policing ordinary modules; tight budgets would generate GATE 8 noise | ADR-0008 |
| D-008 | Phase Gate Checker specified but **not** implemented in Phase 0 | Canonical phase model places implementation in Phase 2; Phase 0 produces no code | Phase 0B |
| D-009 | Golden Repair corpus **defined** but not populated | Corpus instances require an accepted Golden Product to inject into | Phase 0B |
| D-010 | Phase 0 commits as a candidate, explicitly not accepted | Canonical set forbids self-acceptance; commit records work, GATE 1 records acceptance | Phase 0B |
| D-011 | PyYAML used only to validate the authority map parses | Read-only validation of a Phase 0 artifact; no runtime dependency added, no lockfile, no install performed | Phase 0B |
| D-012 | Golden Repair: **definition** at Phase 0B, **instantiation** at Phase 30 | Derived from canonical text, not chosen: BP §Phase 0B says "corpus **definition**" and every sibling item in that list is a definition/specification/declaration/design; MS defines the corpus as "**injected** defects" executed "against a Golden Product revision that has already passed acceptance". Injection requires a target that does not exist before Phase 30 | HG1-02 correction |
| D-013 | Instantiation registered as new ARK-REQ-0187/0188 rather than by amending 0090/0091 | MS §Canonical Requirement Register makes IDs immutable and forbids reuse/renumbering. The reserved gap 0187–0199 in the MS block exists for exactly this | HG1-02 correction |
| D-014 | ARK-REQ-0012 reclassified CONDITIONAL → MANDATORY | MS §Frozen technology direction states "PostgreSQL-ready abstractions" unconditionally. The prior rule made the abstraction inapplicable in the default SQLite deployment — narrowing an unconditional requirement, the exact scope-reduction exploit the register exists to prevent | HG1-03 correction |
| D-015 | Verified *operation* on PostgreSQL is not registered as a requirement | No canonical statement requires it. Registering an unrequired obligation would be as wrong as omitting a required one | HG1-03 correction |
| D-016 | Contract inventory delivered at Phase 0A, not deferred to Phase 2 | BP §Phase 0A lists "contract inventory" explicitly. Phase 2 implements schemas; the inventory is architecture | HG1-01 correction |
| D-017 | Minimal stable-revision pointer primitive delivered **within** Phase 22B, owned by `lifecycle.release` | Recovery Supervisor needs an atomic pointer to a verified immutable revision, not the full release/supply-chain/deployment system. Placing the primitive in 22B removes the deadlock without weakening the rule that Self-Evolution cannot start before verified rollback exists, and without creating a second release authority | HG1-05 correction |
| D-018 | 22B prerequisites = 5, 6, 13, 20 (was 5, 20, 26) | 6 supplies immutable content-addressed revision identity; 13 supplies the "previously verified" record; 5/20 supply snapshot and restore proof. Full Phase 26 is not needed to verify rollback safety | HG1-05 correction |
| D-019 | Dependency validation must enumerate all four edge classes and ship a negative control | The original check used explicit prerequisites only and reported "no cycles" while a real deadlock existed. An edge class omitted from a graph check is a false negative by construction | HG1-05 correction |
| D-020 | Contract definition phase separated from implementation phase | C-03 was required by Phase 2 while implemented at Phase 5 — an impossible forward prerequisite. Phase 2 needs the schema/interface, not the runtime | HG1-06 correction |
| D-021 | Deliverable counts parsed from the canonical Build Protocol lists, never hand-entered | *(historical defect)* an earlier audit read `12/12` while other artifacts read `11/11`, because one canonical bullet had been split into two rows. Current derived counts are 0A 16/16, 0B 11/11 | HG1-08 correction |
| D-022 | Derived numbers are computed at check time, not transcribed | Three artifacts held stale denominators after the register was corrected, including the audit asserting all artifacts agreed. Same root cause as F-0002 | HG1-07 / HG1-09 correction |

## Human rulings incorporated (recorded, not decided here)

| Ruling | Source | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| HUMAN GATE 8 ratified | human authority | Architecture-budget exception is a human gate |
| Direct-AI benchmark states | human authority | `NOT_CONFIGURED` / verified `EXTERNAL_UNAVAILABLE` do not block release; never fabricate an external PASS |
| Phase 0 split 0A/0B | human authority | Two parts, one acceptance package, one gate |
| Workflow derived caches | human authority | Permitted when deterministically derived, hash-bound and invalidated |
| ROLLBACK_STABLE constraints | human authority | Recovery-Supervisor-only, verified immutable target, atomic pointer switch preferred, no transformation |
| Autonomy model | human authority | Machine acceptance for normal phases; stop only at the 8 gates or a failed machine gate |
| **ERR-001 governance erratum** | human authority | `engineering.import` physical `module_root` → `backend/arkali/engineering/project_import`. Physical realizability only: logical identity, authority, lifecycle, TRUST, Protected Core membership and requirement meaning unchanged. Phase 0 not reopened; Stable Core semantics not invoked (no Stable Core exists). Closes F-0015 |
| **Handoff protocol institutionalised** | Phase 2 follow-up | `ARKALI_HANDOFF.md` + `ARKALI_NEW_SESSION_PROMPT.txt` + `scripts/check_handoff.py`. The manifest is an index, never a second authority; every claim it makes is mechanically compared against repository truth and any disagreement is `HANDOFF_DRIFT`. Refresh is mandatory after each accepted phase, gate decision, erratum, promotion, rollback, new BLOCKER/HIGH or change of NEXT EXACT ACTION |
| **HUMAN GATE 1 ACCEPTED** | human authority | Phase 0A + 0B accepted as one package on candidate `007ebf6`; 9 ADRs PROPOSED → ACCEPTED; Phase 1 unlocked. Recorded as `HGR-001`. Autonomous progression through normal phases now applies until GATE 2 (Phase 23) or an earlier gate condition |
| Isolation Backend abstraction | human authority | Properties, not technologies; unsatisfiable ⇒ UNSUPPORTED/DENY; never silently downgrade |
| **State-machine primitive placed in `kernel.contracts`** | Phase 3 implementation | The twelve machines are owned by ten contexts, three of them in the `control` layer. `allow_same_layer: false` means a shared primitive in `control.architecture` could not be imported by `control.registry.project` or `control.registry.provider`. Only layer rank 0 is reachable from every authority, so the *mechanism* is a kernel contract while every *machine* stays owned by the context the authority map names. No universal state-machine object exists |
| **Executable machine definitions are the implementation authority** | Phase 3 implementation | `STATE_MACHINES.md` remains the canonical specification; the twelve executable definitions are the implementation authority for their own machines. Ownership is stated in each module rather than left implicit, and the two are reconciled mechanically on every run, so neither can become a silent private copy of the other |
| **Canonical §6 read literally, not narrowed** | Phase 3 implementation | `any→QUARANTINED` in `STATE_MACHINES.md` §6 is implemented exactly as written, which leaves Plugin Lifecycle with no terminal state. Recorded as F-0018 for human ruling. An implementing actor narrowing a canonical document to something more sensible is precisely the reinterpretation the constitution forbids |
| **ERR-004 — F-0024 confirmed; ARK-REQ-0111 implemented, not reclassified** | human authority | The human ruling refused reclassification, deferral and any weakening of the evidence requirements. The stronger Protected Core profile is now executable in `acceptance.engine`, derives its categories from MS §Protected Core and its membership from `AUTHORITY_MAP`, and cannot be declared or downgraded by the actor making the change. Applied to its own remediation candidate |
| **The profile obligation begins at the phase the register assigns it** | ERR-004 remediation | `ARK-REQ-0111`'s Phase column decides when the stronger profile is owed, so Phases 2 and 3 are NOT_APPLICABLE rather than retroactively in breach. A phase that ran before an obligation existed did not violate it. The boundary is read from the register, never written as a constant |
| **The first execution surface exists; the Phase 4 "no surface" claim is superseded, not withdrawn** | Phase 5 Package 4 | Phase 4 recorded honestly that no execution surface existed and that policy-bypass resistance was therefore CONTRACT-level only, and it planted a tripwire asserting the absence so the claim could not quietly become false. Package 4 built `surfaces.command`, the tripwire fired, and its own message named the obligation: the surface "must be brought under a real PEP with runtime evidence". That is what was delivered — every route enforces through the Phase 4 PEP, every decision lands on the existing audit trail, and a control parses the deployed source and fails if any route skips the guard. The control is replaced rather than relaxed: it now asserts that every surface module that exists is under a real PEP **and** that the five unbuilt surfaces are still absent, so it keeps failing for an unenforced surface. Phase 4's verdict is untouched: its claim was true when made, and bypass resistance across the remaining five paths is still not claimed (ARK-REQ-0325/0347 are Phase 31) |
| **A structural rule is scoped by authority, never by phase** | F-0027 remediation | Six checks have now outlived their phase (F-0008, F-0013, F-0016, F-0019, F-0022, F-0027). The common cause is a rule whose condition is *when* rather than *where*: "no ORM engine yet" expires, "no ORM engine outside the context canonical architecture makes responsible for it" does not. Structure check 12 is restated as an authority rule and the owning context is resolved from `ARCHITECTURE.md` §3 at run time, cross-validated against `AUTHORITY_MAP.yaml`, so no path list exists in the validator to drift. Scope is derived from the declared module roots and covers untracked files, preserving the F-0016 property; unresolvable authority or ownership fails closed rather than passing vacuously |
| **The dependency-direction gate reads `dependency_rules`; it does not model them** | F-0028 remediation | The authority map declared two exceptions the gate never implemented, and `AuthorityMap` did not parse the section at all — a shadow model of the shape ADR-0001 exists to prevent, differing from F-0013 only in failing closed. `edge_permitted` now lives on `AuthorityMap`, beside the data it reads. Exemption subjects are taken from the rule **keys**, so a new exemption is a map edit; resolution is namespace → context final segment → layer, which is load-bearing because `acceptance.engine` shares the `evidence` layer while rule 5 grants the exception to `evidence.*` **by name**. Omitted rules default strict, so absence can never widen the architecture. `evidence_read_for_verdict_only_by` is left unconsumed and said so: it constrains reads *for a verdict*, which an import graph cannot express, and a gate must not claim a scope wider than its field of view |
| **No `control.policy` import was added anywhere** | F-0028 remediation | Correcting the gate makes `kernel.persistence → control.policy` *permissible*; it does not make it *present*. No such import exists and none was introduced, and a control proves the live tree still passes with both exemptions disabled — so the repair cannot be concealing a real violation. Where Phase 5 places its PEP call sites remains a Phase 5 decision, unmade here |
| **GOV-001 enforcement — authorization bound to phase and evidence package** | F-0026 remediation | Whether a phase is already accepted is read from `BUILD_STATE.md` via `GovernanceState`, so no second acceptance history exists. An authorization is a record in `HUMAN_GATE_RECORDS.md`, never an argument: `find_authorization` takes no authorization parameter, so an actor has nowhere to pass one in, and no `--force`/`--rescore`/`authorized=True` exists in the module or the checker. Binding is phase + SHA-256 of `phase_N_report.json` and `phase_N_traceability.json` — identifiers that already existed, so no new identity system was invented. Forbidden issuers are derived from `stable_mutation.prohibited_actors`. Phases 2 and 3 now return `AWAITING_RESCORING_AUTHORITY` on re-run; that is the protection working, and their recorded acceptance is untouched |
| **GOV-001 — superseding re-acceptance rule** | human authority | Ratifies the Phase 4 superseding re-acceptance as VALID; it is not withdrawn. Establishes the standing rule: an accepted phase found defective keeps its historical record immutable and marked superseded; remediation produces a new evidence package; the implementing actor may remediate but may **not** grant itself authority to supersede a prior accepted verdict; re-acceptance requires explicit re-scoring authorization from the human governance authority or a future canonical independent Acceptance Authority; the deterministic checker then performs the re-score, creating a new superseding record; the old commit, evidence and reports are never amended, deleted or concealed. **Rule 6 requires authorization before the re-score — the Phase 4 ordering was remediate-then-report, authorized retrospectively by rule 10, and is not precedent.** Cross-references ERR-004. Enforcement is governance-only; the mechanical gap is F-0026 |
| **A machine re-score of an already-accepted phase is permitted here** *(superseded by GOV-001)* | ERR-004 remediation | Phase 4 is a normal phase (`normal_phase_acceptance: machine`) carrying no human gate. The verdict is issued by the Phase Gate Checker, not by the implementing actor, so `failed_gate_may_be_rescored_by_implementing_actor: false` is not engaged. `VERIFICATION_ARCHITECTURE` §2.2 rule 1 explicitly contemplates supersession, and Phase 1 set the precedent at `1ae0835`. The canonical set does not distinguish re-scoring a rejected phase from re-scoring an accepted one; that gap is recorded in ERR-004 and the position may be overturned, since nothing was overwritten |
| **Phase 4 acceptance is defective and is not treated as valid** *(resolved by ERR-004)* | pre-Phase-5 integrity check | F-0024. `ARK-REQ-0111` was reported as discharged without an implementation; C2 passed on the assertion. Phase 5 was not begun. The verdict at `1ea79f3` is **preserved unamended** rather than rewritten: it is the record of the defect, and `machine_autonomy.failed_gate_may_be_rescored_by_implementing_actor: false` means an implementing actor may not re-score its own accepted phase. The stop is enforced through the canonical mechanism — an open HIGH finding — which now returns `PHASE_BLOCKED` for every gate. Remediation and re-submission are required; reclassifying the requirement instead would need a governance erratum from the acceptance authority |
| **Isolation posture is injected into the PDP, not imported** | Phase 4 implementation | `SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md` §1 shows the PDP reading `control.isolation`. Both are layer rank 1 and `allow_same_layer: false` declares no sibling edge between them, so a direct import would violate the dependency-direction gate. `control.isolation` resolves the posture and it is supplied as a fact on `PolicyRequest`. The PDP stays pure and deterministic and the layering rule holds. The alternative — adding a sibling edge — would have widened the architecture to fit the implementation |
| **ROLLBACK_STABLE is DENY for every actor at Phase 4** | Phase 4 implementation | The canonical set carves out one exception: `lifecycle.recovery` through a **verified** Recovery Supervisor, which is Phase 22B. Granting anything to that invoker now would grant it to a component that does not exist and whose canonical preconditions — verified immutable target, no transformation, evidence emitted — cannot be checked. The invoker is still read from authority so the refusal names it |
| **Security taxonomy split across owning contexts** | Phase 4 implementation | Placing all twelve security error types in `kernel.contracts` pushed that context to 45 public symbols against a budget of 40. The budget was right: the kernel was becoming a dumping ground. Only the shared `SecurityError` base stays in the kernel — needed because `control.policy` and `control.isolation` may not import each other — and the concrete types moved to the contexts that raise them |
| **ERR-002 — Plugin `REMOVED` is terminal** | human authority | Closes F-0018. `any→QUARANTINED` in `STATE_MACHINES.md` §6 is narrowed to `any pre-REMOVED→QUARANTINED` with an explicit `Forbidden: REMOVED→any`. A removed plugin revision cannot be quarantined again, reactivated or reinstalled by mutating the same instance; reintroduction starts a new lifecycle with its own provenance. No state added or removed; the six legal quarantine paths are asserted unchanged. Phase 0 not reopened, Phase 3 remains MACHINE-ACCEPTED |
| **ERR-003 — architecture-budget measurement contract** | human authority | Closes F-0020. A budget participating in acceptance must have exactly one deterministic measurement definition. Ratified in `AUTHORITY_MAP.yaml` `architecture_budget_measurement` v1.0.0: McCabe `decision_points + 1` per function with the incrementing nodes enumerated as data, and orchestration depth as the longest directed chain over the bounded-context graph per `ARCHITECTURE.md` §8. No budget value changed. Not a second authority — the contract sits beside the values it measures. Re-measurement exposed three real violations including one in accepted Phase 2 code; all repaired by decomposition, none grandfathered, no GATE 8 requested |
| **Two budgets left unenforced pending a canonical formula** *(superseded by ERR-003)* | Phase 3 implementation | `max_cyclomatic_complexity_per_function` and `max_orchestration_depth` are declared as numbers with no measurement rule. ADR-0008 forbids a budget exception resting on a justification authored by an implementing actor; authoring the measurement rule that decides whether an exception is needed falls under the same prohibition. Recorded as F-0020, named in the gate's evidence detail, and neither silently enforced nor silently dropped |
